sources.title: Pro-PRC "HaiEnergy" Information Operations Campaign Leverages Infrastructure from Public Relations Firm to Disseminate Content on Inauthentic News Sites
Pro-PRC HaiEnergy Campaign Exploits U.S. News Outlets via Newswire Services to Target U.S. Audiences; Evidence of Commissioned Protests in Washington, D.C.

notes: Mandiant 2022 says it lacks sufficient evidence to determine how far Haixun is involved in, or aware of, HaiEnergy; 'linked to' is kept as stated and no state principal is named. Table 2 lists 72 sites (59 domains plus 13 subdomains); the 59 apex domains are given, subdomains (for example markets.charmdaily.com) omitted. Several names imitate real outlets (thekoreatimes.org, jakartaglobe.org, thewarsawvoice.com); Mandiant lists them as Haixun-linked sites, not as the real outlets. Mandiant 2023 found content placed via Times Newswire and World Newswire onto subdomains of US outlets that point to FinancialContent infrastructure; those US outlets were not compromised and are excluded. 'paid influencers' rests on Haixun's Fiverr commissions (s2); 'paid placement in real media' rests on the newswire placements (s2). Mandiant also assesses the campaign may have financed two small protests in Washington, D.C. in 2022 (s2). 'forged documents' rests on fabricated letters about Adrian Zenz (s1).

name: Sponsored Discontent
operator: Unknown; bylines in some published articles connected the author to Jilin Yousen Culture Communication Co, Ltd

attributions.says: Likely China-origin ChatGPT accounts generating social media content in English and long-form articles in Spanish

narratives: Short English and Chinese posts attacking dissident Cai Xia, and Spanish long-form articles portraying US inequality, violence, drug use and homelessness as signs of failed American leadership, published around the 2024 APEC forum in Peru.

sources.title: Disrupting malicious uses of our models: an update February 2025

notes: OpenAI notes overlap with Spamouflage for the Cai Xia comments but treats this as a distinct line of effort. The Latin American outlets that published the articles (La Republica, Wapa, El Popular, Libero, Extra, Expreso, El Universal, El Plural) are real outlets and are excluded; at least one article was marked 'patrocinado' (sponsored), and OpenAI says some publications may have resulted from a financial arrangement. The company named in bylines is recorded as a byline fact, not as OpenAI's attribution of the operator. 'content laundering' rests on translating and expanding public Chinese-language articles into Spanish. OpenAI rates it Category 4 on the Breakout Scale. No indicators published.

name: Sneer Review

attributions.says: Likely China-origin activity generating social media content and internal reviews

narratives: Critical comments and a fake 'backlash' article about a Taiwanese anti-CCP board game, a false pornography claim against Baloch activist Mahrang Baloch, and both-sided comments on the USAID shutdown tied to US tariffs.

sources.title: Disrupting malicious uses of AI: June 2025

notes: One user claimed in a prompt to work for the Chinese Propaganda Department; OpenAI says it has no independent evidence for this, so it is not used as an attribution. The accounts also drafted an internal performance review describing the operation, and an essay styled as a public security document. 'fake news outlets' rests on two Facebook Pages posing as news outlets. Dates: report published June 2025 and content references the 2025 USAID closure; no start date given. No indicators published.

name: VAGue Focus

attributions.says: Likely China-origin activity focused on social engineering in US and Europe
attributions.section: Social engineering meets IO: Operation "VAGue Focus", p.17

narratives: Personas posing as European or Turkey-based journalists and analysts for 'Focus Lens News', 'BrightWave Media Europe' and 'Visionary Advisory Group' sought information on US economic and financial policy, including paid interview offers and offers to pay for classified documents.

sources.title: Disrupting malicious uses of AI: June 2025

notes: OpenAI says the operators themselves described the entities as fronts for intelligence collection. OpenAI identified nine X accounts and one domain but names neither, so no indicators are listed. 'hijacked or bought accounts' rests on OpenAI's note that the Focus Lens News X account (created 2014, dormant until mid-2024) is typical of compromised and repurposed accounts. Start year 2024 rests on that mid-2024 reactivation.

name: Uncle Spam

attributions.says: We banned a number of ChatGPT accounts linked to a China-origin influence operation following a lead from our peers at Meta.

narratives: Polarised posts on both sides of US debates, chiefly for and against tariffs, including fictitious US veteran personas critical of the administration.

sources.title: Disrupting malicious uses of AI: June 2025

notes: OpenAI ties this to the threat actor in Meta's original 2022 report (see meta-2022-09-china-us-czechia). The accounts also sought code to scrape profile data from X and Bluesky. 'AI-generated images' rests on AI-made logos used as profile pictures, such as 'Veterans for Justice'. Language 'en' is inferred from the US-facing samples. No indicators published.

name: Nine—emdash Line

attributions.says: potentially affiliated with a covert influence operation originating from China

narratives: English posts on Vietnam's alleged environmental damage in the South China Sea and claims that Philippine President Marcos used drugs and manipulated elections, plus Cantonese posts branding Hong Kong pro-democracy figures (Jimmy Lai, Nathan Law, Agnes Chow) criminals or traitors.

sources.title: Disrupting malicious uses of AI: an update (October 2025)

notes: OpenAI says the accounts resembled Spamouflage but it found no technical links. 'yue' (Cantonese) is ISO 639-3; no ISO 639-1 code exists, and 'zh' would lose the distinction. The Marcos video was not generated by OpenAI models and the Philippine government called it a deepfake or digitally altered; 'deepfake' is not listed as an operation technique because OpenAI does not say the operation made it. The October 2025 report's other China section covers PRC-linked surveillance and phishing requests, not covert IO; 'Stop News' in that report is Russia-origin.
